title: Establishment of Kidney Cancer Organoid Cultures
protocol: Pre-warm tissue culture plates overnight at 37°C.
Thaw Matrigel on ice several hours or overnight before use.
Wash RCC tissue specimens and remove fatty and necrotic tissue.
Mince the tissue biopsy into small pieces of < 1 mm³ size using a scalpel.
Transfer minced tissue in 10 ml PBS to a 50 ml falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C, then aspirate supernatant and weigh the pellet.
Weigh the empty Falcon tube before transferring the tissue.
Prepare one ml of 2 mg/ml Collagenase P solution per 50 mg of tissue.
Digest the tissue at 37°C for approximately 30 minutes, rocking gently.
Wash with 25 ml PBS and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the sample in 5 ml of PBS, and filter the cell suspension through a 70 µm followed by a 40 µm cell strainer.
Wash the filters 3x with PBS.
Centrifuge the eluate at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash the cell pellet with PBS.
Incubate in 5 ml of RBC erythrocyte lysis buffer for 5 min at RT.
After washing in PBS, count the cells using a hemocytometer and resuspend in 80 µl MACS buffer per 1 x 10^7 cells.
Add 20 µl of anti-CD45 Microbeads per 80 µl of cell suspension and incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash the cells in 2 ml of MACS buffer per 1 x 10^7 cells before resuspending the pellet in 500 µl of MACS buffer per 1 x 10^8 cells.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to achieve a concentration of 1.25 mg/ml.
After magnetic separation of CD45+ white blood cells using a 30 µm pre-separation filter and MACS buffer equilibrated MS column, collect the flow-through containing CD45- cells.
Wash the column three times with 500 μl of MACS buffer.
Centrifuge the CD45- cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pelleted CD45- cells in PBS and count the viable (unstained) cells by mixing 10 µl of Trypan Blue solution with 10 µl cell solution.
Resuspend 1.5 x 10^4 cells per well in pre-chilled growth medium before adding Matrigel to a final concentration of 75%.
Plate 25 μl drops of the cell-Matrigel mixture in the middle of each well on a pre-heated 48-well plate.
Place the tissue culture plate upside down in the CO₂ incubator for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Gently add 250 µl of pre-warmed organoid growth medium into each well.
Place the plate into a CO₂ incubator (5% CO₂, 37°C).
Refresh the medium every 2-3 days.
Check organoid growth daily using a brightfield microscope.
Passage the organoids when they reach a diameter of 300-500 µm.
Using a 1 ml pipette tip, release organoids from Matrigel lenses by pipetting up and down several times.
Transfer released organoids to a 15 ml falcon tube coated with 1% BSA in PBS (w/v).
Wash the wells with 1 ml of PBS to obtain all cells, and add them to the falcon tube.
Harvest the organoids in at least 5 ml of total volume.
Pipette thoroughly using a 100 µl tip on a 5 ml serological pipet to fully release the organoids from the Matrigel.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer to eliminate dead cells, cells not within the growing organoids or without organoid formation potential.
Wash the strainer with 5 ml of growth medium and invert the cell strainer onto a 10 cm^2 dish.
Wash retained organoids from the membrane with 10 ml of growth medium.
Collect organoids in a 15 ml falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and Matrigel above the pellet.
Resuspend organoids in 300-500 µl of TrypLE Select cell dissociation enzyme solution.
Incubate for 5-15 min at room temperature with frequent perturbation by pipetting.
Check organoid dispersion under a bright-field microscope.
Stop the digestion by adding 4 ml of growth medium.
Centrifuge the organoids at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the organoids in pre-chilled growth medium.
Add Matrigel to a final concentration of 75%.
Plate 25 µl drops containing the Matrigel and cells in the middle of the well of a pre-heated 48-well plate.
Place the tissue culture plate upside down in the CO₂ incubator for 20 min at 37°C.
Gently add 250 µl of pre-warmed organoid growth medium into each well.
Place the plate back into the CO₂ incubator (5% CO₂, 37°C).
Refresh the medium every 2-3 days.
Check organoid growth daily using a brightfield microscope.
Release the organoids from Matrigel and dissociate them into clusters for cryopreservation.
Cryopreserve organoids as clusters instead of whole organoids to increase reformation and viability.
Resuspend the organoid clusters in 1 ml of Recovery Cell Culture Freezing Medium per 2-3 wells of the dissociated organoids, and transfer to cryotubes.
Freeze the cryostocks for at least 6 hours in isopropanol containers at -80°C before storage in liquid nitrogen.
Thaw the cells in a 37°C water bath when ready to culture them.
Shake the vial until only a small piece of ice remains and quickly continue processing the cells.
Transfer the thawed cells into a 15 ml falcon tube.
Dropwise add 10 ml of pre-warmed growth medium to the falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 75% Matrigel.
Release the organoids from Matrigel as described in steps 3 i-iii.
Centrifuge the organoids at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C, and discard the supernatant, including Matrigel and dead cells.
Wash the organoids with 0.1% BSA in PBS (w/v), and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the organoids in 7 ml of 10% NBF in PBS (v/v), and fix overnight at 4°C rocking.
Wash the organoids with 0.1% BSA in PBS (w/v), resuspend in 500-1000 μl of 0.1% BSA in PBS (w/v), transfer to a coated 2 ml Eppendorf tube, and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Place the tube in an 80°C heating block briefly before carefully overlaying the organoid pellet with 400 μl of 1.5% agarose.
Centrifuge shortly at 300 x g at 4°C.
Place the tube in the centrifuge in the same orientation as before.
After the agarose has polymerized, release the agarose bead from the Eppendorf tube.
Use a razor blade to cut off the bottom of the Eppendorf tube at the opposite side as the organoid pellet.
Carefully push out the agarose bead.
Trim the bead around the organoid pellet.
Transfer the trimmed bead to an embedding cassette.
Place the cassette in 70% EtOH for 24-48 h.
Dehydrate the organoids according to Table 2.
After embedding in paraffin, section the paraffin-embedded organoids using a microtome at 5 µm thickness with a water bath at a temperature of 48°C.
Quickly transfer the sections onto glass slides.
Place air-dried glass slides on a 60°C warming block for 15 min.
Place the slides in a 60°C oven for 60 min to fix organoids to the glass slide.
Rehydrate the organoids before performing hematoxylin and eosin staining.
Perform immunocytochemistry after rehydration.
Submerge the organoids in 80% EtOH for 30 min.
Transfer the organoids to 90% EtOH for 30 min.
Place the organoids in 96% EtOH for 1 h.
Incubate the organoids in 100% EtOH for 1 h.
Continue incubation of organoids in 100% EtOH for 30 min.
Soak the organoids in toluene for 1 h.
Transfer the organoids to a new toluene solution for 30 min.
Immerse the organoids in paraffin for 1-3 h.
Keep the organoids in paraffin overnight.
Incubate the organoids in paraffin for an additional 1 h.
Release the organoids from Matrigel as described previously.
Resuspend the released organoids in 1500 µl of 10% NBF in PBS.
Transfer the resuspended organoids to a 2 ml coated Eppendorf tube.
Fix the organoids for 1.5 h at 4°C while shaking.
Wash the fixed organoids five times with PBS-T over 2 h at 4°C while shaking.
Block with 1% BSA in PBS-T containing 10% donkey serum for 2 hours at room temperature shaking.
Prepare antibody dilutions in 1% BSA in PBS-T.
Incubate the organoids with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C shaking.
Wash the organoids 4 times with PBS-T over 4 hours at 4°C shaking with centrifugation at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with secondary antibodies and DAPI overnight at 4°C shaking.
Wrap the Eppendorf tubes in aluminum foil to prevent fluorophore photobleaching.
The next day, wash the organoids 6 times with PBS-T over 6 hours at 4°C shaking with centrifugation at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the organoids in PBS-T.
Add an equal amount of 2% low-melting agarose to distribute the organoids well in solution before transfer.
Transfer the organoids to an 8-well chambered cover-glass slide for confocal fluorescence microscopy.
Release the organoids from Matrigel as described in steps 3| i-iii.
Resuspend the organoids in 7 ml of 2% (w/v) paraformaldehyde and 2.5% (v/v) glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M phosphate buffer.
Fix the organoids for 2h at RT shaking, and wash 2x with 0.1 M phosphate buffer for 15 min.
Resuspend the organoids in 500 - 1000 µl 0.1 M phosphate buffer, transfer them to a coated 2 ml Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Short place the tube in an 80°C heating block before carefully overlaying the organoid pellet with 400 μl of 10% agarose.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 10 s.
Post-fix samples with 1% (v/v) osmium tetroxide.
Dehydrate samples in a graded series of ethanol.
Embed samples in PolyBed® 812 resin.
Stain ultrathin sections, 60-80 nm thick, with uranyl acetate and lead citrate.
Examine stained sections at 80 kV with an electron microscope.
Release organoid-Matrigel lenses from the well using a 1 ml pipette tip.
Transfer released organoids to an uncoated 15 ml falcon tube.
Wash the wells with 1 ml of PBS.
Add washed cells to the Falcon tube containing organoids.
Pipette thoroughly using a 100 µl tip on a 5 ml serological pipet to release the organoids from the Matrigel.
Centrifuge the organoids at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C, and discard the supernatant, including Matrigel and dead cells.
Wash the organoids with ice cold PBS, and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the organoids in 500-1000 µl of ice-cold PBS, transfer to a 2 ml Eppendorf tube, and centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Mix the organoid pellet with 5 ml of Cell Recovery Solution.
Incubate for 1h at 4°C rotating.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 300 x g at 4°C, remove the supernatant.
Wash the organoid pellet twice with ice cold PBS.
Transfer the organoid pellet to an Eppendorf tube using PBS.
Resuspend organoids in 100 µl of RIPA buffer containing protease and/or phosphatase inhibitors.
Lysate organoids for 10 min on ice.
Centrifuge lysed organoids at 15,000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Store supernatant at -20°C after total protein measurement by Bradford assay.
Release the organoids from Matrigel as described in steps 3| i-iii.
Resuspend the organoids in 300-500 µl of TrypLE Select cell dissociation enzyme solution.
Incubate for 15-30 min at room temperature with frequent perturbation by pipetting.
Check organoid dispersion under a bright-field microscope.
Resuspend 5000 single cells per well in pre-chilled medium.
Add Matrigel to a final concentration of 75% Matrigel.
Plate 9 μl cell-Matrigel drops in the middle of each well of a pre-heated 96-well plate.
Invert the plates and incubate at 37°C for 20 min to allow the Matrigel containing cells to solidify.
Mark the position of any Matrigel drops that are not plated exactly in the middle of the wells on the lid.
Mark the position of any Matrigel drops attached to the side of the well.
Mix 100 µl of pre-warmed organoid growth medium into each well.
Place the plate into a CO₂ incubator (5% CO₂, 37°C).
Cultivate the organoids with inhibitors for 7 days according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Resuspend CellTiter Glo Substrate in CellTiter Glo Buffer.
Add the solution to the cell cultures in a 1:2 dilution.
Incubate for 10 min at RT before recording luminescence.
